title: S4 E9 shed-ladder port scoping has no cross-direction discriminator test
detail: The re-keyed ladder's candidate scan is port-scoped, but no fixture loads the reverse port with sheddable packets — a partial-revert to bundle-wide scanning stays green. Only bound pooling is mutation-pinned.
recommended_fix: Extend test_e9_bound_is_per_port: load the reverse port's Best-effort lane, send an Express arrival to the at-bound forward port; assert the shed comes from the arrival's own port (or the arrival itself), never the reverse port.

title: S4 crisis resolve measures' direction keying unpinned — unidirectional fixtures only
evidence:
crisis.odin 420-424: `relieved := bound > margin &&
			port_class_queue(state, cat, b, ac.dir, ac.class) + margin < bound &&
			!port_lane_at(state, cat, b, ac.dir, bound - margin)
		cleared = relieved &&
			!drop_of_class_this_tick(state, ac.class, .Queue_Overflow, b, ac.dir, true)` — plus port_class_queue's own filter (crisis.odin:128): `if port_dir_of_packet(state, p) != dir { continue }`. Every resolve-path fixture seeds one direction only (crisis_test.odin:232-235, test_crisis_resolve_and_retrigger): `for tk in u64(1200)..<3000 {
		if tk % 2 == 0 {
			flow_seed_demand(&s.flow, tk, h, r, 1)`; grep for HI_TO_LO/reverse/opposite across crisis_test.odin and qos_test.odin returns zero hits — no same-bundle bidirectional crisis fixture exists.
detail: Deleting the dir filters in port_class_queue/port_lane_at, or dropping dir_ok=true, is invisible on unidirectional fixtures — all resolve arcs (retrigger, margin clamp, lane threshold) stay green. The cross-port relief discriminator is untested.
recommended_fix: Add a resolve fixture with same-pair opposite-direction load: an other-direction shed must not block relief (dir_ok gate) and other-direction backlog must not count toward this port's relieved check.

title: Q-row CSV literal not pinned — column-swap guard test not extended to the new row kind
detail: The Q row's column order is unpinned: a field swap in the Q printf passes every test (both live and replay would carry the same wrong bytes) — exactly the failure class this guard exists for.
recommended_fix: Append a hand-built Stats_Port_Row (recognizable values, e.g. router=3, peer=9, dir=1, q={2,0,6}, util=42) and one strings.contains literal "Q,7,3,9,1,2,0,6,42\n" to test_stats_csv_literal_rows.
